svg.title: What the model sees before it starts
svg.desc: Horizontal stacked bar chart of the first-call context footprint in tokens for three harnesses on the same model (Claude Sonnet 4.5, MCP off, no loaded memory or user skills, fresh session). Copilot CLI totals ~16.2k tokens (system instructions ~6.9k, tool definitions ~9.0k, environment 100, first user request 147). Claude CLI totals ~29.5k tokens (system instructions ~7.6k, tool definitions ~20.4k across all 27 tools sent upfront, first user request ~1.4k); tool definitions dominate at roughly 69 percent. VS Code agent totals ~18.5k tokens (system instructions ~4.9k, tool definitions ~10.1k, environment ~1.8k, skill descriptions ~1.2k, repository instructions 348, memory 102, first user request 34). Tool definitions are the largest component everywhere: about 56 percent of the Copilot CLI prefix, 69 percent of the Claude CLI prefix, and 54 percent of the VS Code prefix. All three totals use the same Anthropic tokenizer (uncached input plus cache-read plus cache-creation) and are directly comparable; the spread is about 1.82 times.
svg.text: What the model sees before it starts
First-call context footprint in tokens (Claude Sonnet 4.5, same model; MCP off, no skills or loaded memory; fresh session).
Total input tokens the model tokenizes on the first request — uncached + cache-read + cache-creation, same Anthropic tokenizer. Legend numbers: Copilot CLI · Claude CLI · VS Code.
Tool definitions are the largest component everywhere: ~56% of the Copilot CLI prefix, ~69% of Claude CLI's, ~54% of VS Code's.

Bars are exact first-call totals (one Anthropic tokenizer). Copilot CLI and VS Code splits from captured payloads; Claude CLI split is its structural proportions scaled to the exact total. Claude CLI sends all 27 tools upfront.
